Application Materials.content:
As part of your online application, you also need to submit the following supporting documents:
- A copy (or copies) of your official degree certificate(s) (if you have already completed your degree)
- A copy (or copies) of your official academic transcript(s), showing full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained
- Official English translations of the certificate(s) and transcript(s)
- One reference letter on headed paper
- Evidence of your English language ability (if your first language is not English)
- Any additional documents required for this programme (see Entry requirements for this programme)
- A copy of the photo page of your passport
You have **42 days** to submit your application once you begin the process. You may save and return to your application as many times as you wish to update information, complete sections or upload supporting documents such as your final transcript or your language test. For more information about submitting documents or other topics related to applying to a postgraduate taught programme, see [how to apply for a postgraduate taught degree](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/how-to-apply-for-a-postgraduate-taught-degree/).
**Reference**: Please provide one reference. This should typically be an academic reference but in cases where this is not possible then a reference from a current employer may be accepted instead. Certain programmes, such as the MBA programme, may also accept an employer reference. If you already have a copy of a reference on letter headed paper then please upload this to your application. If you do not already have a reference to upload then please enter your referee’s name and contact details on the online application and we will contact your referee directly.
Employment and Experience: Please complete this section as fully as possible with all employments relevant to your course. Additional details may be attached in your personal statement/proposal where appropriate.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Standard entry requirements:** **2.1 Hons (or non-UK equivalent)** in Business, Management or another subject with a quantitative focus.
- Applicants with a **2:1 degree or non-UK equivalent in an unrelated subject area** and **at least two years of relevant work experience** will be considered on an individual basis.
- This is a conversion course for students who have no previous studies in the area of Business Analytics.
- **China-specific academic entry requirements:** Bachelor degree at **70%/75%/80%/85%/87%** depending on university attended — see “Result Required 2.1” on the [China University Grade Equivalences List](https://www.gla.ac.uk/media/Media_1221495_smxx.pdf) — in Business, Management or another subject with a quantitative focus.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
For applicants from non-English speaking countries, as defined by the [UK Government](https://www.gov.uk/student-visa/knowledge-of-english), the University sets a minimum English Language proficiency level.
- **IELTS Academic and Academic Online (not General Training): 6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. IELTS One Skill Retake Accepted. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **TOEFL (ibt, mybest or athome)**, tests taken up to 20 January 2026: **90 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 20; Listening 19; Speaking 19; Writing 21. Tests taken from 21 January 2026: **92 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 22; Listening 20; Speaking 23; Writing 21. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test, this includes TOEFL mybest.
- **Pearsons PTE Academic: 65 overall** with no subtest less than Reading 60; Listening 60; Speaking 65; Writing 60. Online PTE not accepted for entry. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Cambridge Proficiency in English (CPE) and Cambridge Advanced English (CAE): 176 overall with no subtest less than 169**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Oxford English Test: 7 overall with no subtest less than 6**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **LanguageCert Academic/ Academic Online: 70 overall with no subtest less than 65**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Password Skills Plus: 6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Trinity College Integrated Skills in English II:** two subtests at **96 or higher**, and two subtests at **80 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Kaplan Test of English:** any two subtests at **480 or higher**, and any two subtests at **450 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **University of Glasgow Pre-sessional courses:** tests are accepted for **2 years** following date of successful completion.
Alternatives to English Language qualification:
- Degree from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English): students must have studied for a minimum of their final year at Undergraduate level, or **9 months at Master's level**, and must have completed their degree in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
- Undergraduate 2+2 and 3+1 degrees from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English): students must have completed their final year of study in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
For international students, the Home Office has confirmed that the University can choose to use these tests to make its own assessment of English language ability for visa applications to degree level programmes. The University is also able to accept UKVI approved Secure English Language Tests (SELT) but does not require a specific UKVI SELT for degree level programmes; it still accepts any of the English tests listed for admission to this programme.
The University of Glasgow accepts evidence of the required language level from the English for Academic Study Unit Pre-sessional courses. Pre-sessional courses give successful students direct entry to the University programme with no need to take IELTS. More information: [Pre-sessional courses](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mlc/eas/pre-sessionalcourses/). The University can also consider pre-sessional courses accredited by BALEAP approved institutions to meet the language requirements for admission to postgraduate taught degrees: Heriot Watt, Kingston Upon Thames, Middlesex University, Manchester University, Reading University, Edinburgh University, ST Andrews University, UCL, Durham.
As part of the online application, applicants need to submit evidence of English language ability if their first language is not English. In the online application guidance, under **English Language Proficiency**, applicants should state the date of any English language test taken (or to be taken) and the award date (or expected award date if known).

Program Overview.content:
The Masters in Business Analytics is designed to help you stay competitive in a data-driven world. You will learn how to turn data into valuable insights that drive business success, and gain practical skills to enhance decision-making, optimise business performance and drive innovation. This programme gives you the tools you need to excel in today’s business environment to make a real impact. It provides flexibility to suit your interests and career goals, allowing you to customise your learning path with optional courses.
- **Teaching start:** September
- [Glasgow: Gilmorehill campus](https://www.gla.ac.uk/explore/campuses/gilmorehill/)
- **MSc:** 12 months full-time
- Build practical skills to solve real-world business challenges in a dynamic and blended learning environment.
- Develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills that are highly valued by employers, giving you a competitive edge.
- Explore key topics like statistical analysis, data mining, predictive modelling, and machine learning with a focus on practical business use.
- Benefit from career development tools, mentoring, and industry connections to help you succeed in business analytics and related fields.
- Get hands-on experience with tools like Python, Tableau, SQL, and R. Learn to analyse real-world data, optimise processes, and uncover insights with expert support.
- Gain valuable experience by working with live clients on [industry projects](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/business-analytics/?card=industryprojects). Bridge classroom theory with practical, real-world applications. *Industry Projects are not guaranteed. All applications are subject to availability and review processes. We will support candidates with their applications before the deadline but if unsuccessful, they can opt for a research proposal for their dissertation. Students can also secure their own projects with approval from academic and/or professional services.*
[Adam Smith Business School is **triple accredited**](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/business/aboutus/accreditationsandrankings/accreditations/ "Home » Schools » Adam Smith Business School » About us » Accreditations and rankings » Accreditations").
You will take four core and a selection of optional courses, delivered across two semesters. Optional courses are tailored to deepen your knowledge in key areas, while offering the opportunity to specialise. During the summer term, you will undertake a significant piece of work through the Applied Project in Business Analytics. This project enables you to apply the skills and knowledge gained during the year to real-world business challenges, preparing you for a successful career in the field of business analytics.
Graduates are well-prepared for careers as Business Analysts, Data Analysts, Data Scientists, Operations Analysts, Market Research Analysts, and Quantitative Consultants. These roles are available across various sectors, including finance, healthcare, technology, retail, and manufacturing, making graduates highly adaptable and in demand.
This is a conversion course for students who have no previous studies in the area of Business Analytics.

Multiple Applications.content:
- Parallel applications to multiple programmes will be dealt with as separate applications at all times.
- Applicants must make a new application for each programme they want to be considered for.
- Applicants may accept more than one conditional offer but can only accept one unconditional offer.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
It may be possible to defer your offer to the next available intake. Deferral requests will be considered individually and are not guaranteed.
Deferral requests for the 2027 intake are open. To be considered for a deferral, you must have accepted a conditional or unconditional offer for the 2027 intake and have paid any relevant deposits to secure your place on the course. The deadline for requesting a deferral to the 2027 intake is **30 September 2026**. If you do not meet these criteria, your request will declined.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
To accept a conditional offer:
- Log in to [Applicant Self-Service](https://uogapply.mycampus.gla.ac.uk/psc/campus/EMPLOYEE/SA/c/CY2_AD_MENU.CY2_AD_NUR_FL.GBL&cmd=start?CAMPUS_URL=https%3a%2f%2fuogapply.mycampus.gla.ac.uk%3a443%2fpsp%2fcampus%2fEMPLOYEE%2fSA%2fs%2fWEBLIB_SCC_NUR.SCC_SS_GATEKEEPER.FieldFormula.IScript_SCC_GateKeeper%3fSCC_APPL_CONTXT_ID%3dSCC_NURCTXT_20171218163641).
- Go to the Application(s) tile and select your programme.
- Click on Accept.
- You will be asked to upload the required documents through Applicant-Self-Service to meet the conditions of your offer. Your offer letter will list all the conditions that apply to your offer. You can also find these conditions on your 'To Do' list within Applicant-Self-Service where you can also upload the required document(s).
- Once documents are uploaded, the items on your 'To do' list in Applicant Self-Service will not instantly disappear; an admissions officer must review the documents and update the status of your application.
- You should normally see an update to your 'To do' list within **5 working days**. If all the conditions of your offer have been met then you will be issued with an unconditional offer letter by email.
- You must accept the unconditional offer even if a conditional offer was accepted previously.
